study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study applied normative modeling to morphometric similarity in a longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia to investigate cross-sectional and longitudinal heterogeneity of structural connectivity.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset; representative: aomic; camcan; dlbs; ixi; narratives; oasis3; rockland; sald; Utrecht Schizophrenia project; GROUP consortium
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists the 11 datasets used for the analysis. The answer follows the guide's instruction for reporting more than five datasets.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Eleven datasets were combined to create the full sample. These datasets are described in Fig. 1, including the sample size, age, and sex distribution of each dataset. We included healthy participants from ten publicly available datasets: the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (aomic) (id1000, piop1 and piop2) datasets, the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (camcan) dataset, the Dallas Longitudinal Brain Study (dlbs) dataset, the Information eXtraction from Images (ixi) dataset (http://braindevelopment.org/ixidataset/), the Narratives (narratives) dataset, the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (oasis3) dataset, the NKI-Rockland (rockland) dataset and the Southwest University adult lifespan (sald) dataset. One dataset is not publicly available and consisted of a large longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-68 years (at baseline) from the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Automated and manual QC. Automated: Euler number thresholding (>10 from centered mean) resulted in 29 exclusions. For the clinical sample, additional non-visual QC metrics (SNR, CNR, etc.) based on the PCP protocol were used with outlier removal (mean - 2.698 * SD). Manual: Visual QC for the clinical sample. The Euler number was also included as a covariate in the normative models.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: The Freesurfer Euler number was extracted as a proxy for image quality. Subjects were removed if the maximum, absolute, within-dataset centered Euler number was larger than 10, and 29 subjects were removed... For the clinical sample, we applied extensive visual and non-visual image quality control procedures... In order to reduce residual variance due to differences in image quality across subjects, we decided to include the Euler number as a variable in our normative models.
rci8_quality_checking.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Image processing and quality control, and Normative modeling of morphometric similarity

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score. A z-score ≥ 1.96 was considered supra-normal and ≤ -1.96 was infra-normal. The total number of outlier regions (total outlier count) and the change in z-scores over time (z-diff) were also used.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper clearly defines the deviation metric as a z-score, specifies the thresholds for supra- and infra-normal, and also describes derived metrics like total outlier count and z-diff.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: For each individual deviation (z) scores, quantifying individual deviation from the normative range, were calculated... we considered a z-score ≥ 1.96 as supra-normal and a z-score ≤ -1.96 as infra-normal... Here we determine the change over time in the total number of outlier regions per participant... Differences in z-scores over time by region are calculated by implementing the z-diff approach...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons (schizophrenia vs. healthy controls) on network-level z-scores, regional z-score changes (z-diff), and total outlier counts were performed using Welch t-tests. Proportions of individuals with extreme z-scores were compared using two-proportions z-tests. Associations between deviation metrics (z-scores, outlier counts) and clinical scores (IQ, PANSS) were tested using Pearson correlations. Group comparisons on continuous variables were FDR corrected.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study found decreased morphometric similarity in the default mode network (DMN) in individuals with schizophrenia, but longitudinal analysis showed that these abnormalities were not progressive over time compared to healthy controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: At baseline, individuals with schizophrenia showed significantly increased morphometric similarity in the somatomotor network (d=0.30) and decreased similarity in the default mode network (DMN) (d=-0.36) compared to controls. However, the percentage of individuals with extreme deviations (infra- or supra-normal z-scores) was small (<6%) and similar to controls. Longitudinally, there were no significant group differences in the change of regional z-scores or the total number of outlier regions over time, suggesting that morphometric similarity abnormalities in chronic schizophrenia are not progressive.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The training dataset lacked diversity (primarily European ancestry). The modeling approach treated brain regions as independent, ignoring potential correlations. Normative modeling itself cannot establish disease specificity. The clinical sample size, while comparable to other studies, could be larger to increase statistical power.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: This study has limitations. For clinical translation... larger and more heterogeneous datasets, incorporating not solely European ancestry data, are imperative... The normative modeling framework employed herein treats each region as independent... by definition, normative models can only detect deviations from the norm but not whether these are specific to a particular condition... While our sample size of individuals with schizophrenia was comparable to previous normative modeling stu... [truncated]

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study directly compared the normative modeling approach (using z-scores) to a traditional analysis of 'raw' morphometric similarity values, finding that the normative model produced results with greater statistical significance for group differences.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is the first study to apply a longitudinal normative modeling framework to morphometric similarity.
